title: Quotes, Citations & Inline Code 💬
description: Blockquotes, inline quotes, abbreviations, and displaying code snippets.

slides.title: Quoting Text 💬
slides.content:
# Blockquotes and Inline Quotes - `
` – a longer, block‑level quote (usually indented). - `` – an inline quote that automatically adds quotation marks. ```html

Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.

— Oscar Wilde

She said HTML is easier than it looks.

```

slides.title: Citing Sources with `<cite>` 📚
slides.content:
# Give Credit Use `` to mark the title of a creative work (book, movie, painting). It typically renders in italic. ```html

My favourite book is The Great Gatsby.

``` Don't use `` for a person's name – it's for the **work**.

quizData.question: Which tag automatically adds quotation marks around the text?
quizData.explanation: The `<q>` element inserts language‑appropriate quotation marks automatically.

slides.title: Abbreviations & Acronyms 🅰️
slides.content:
# Explain Jargon

Use `<abbr>` for abbreviations and provide the full form in the `title` attribute. A tooltip shows the expansion.

```html
<abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>
```
Hovering over "HTML" will display the full term. Great for accessibility.

slides.title: Address & Time
slides.content: Although we'll cover more semantics later, `<address>` is for contact info, and `<time>` for dates/times:
slides.codeSnippet:
Written by John.
Visit us at: 123 Web St.

Published on June 1, 2025.

slides.title: Displaying Code: `<code>` & Friends ⌨️
slides.content:
# Show Code in Your Page - `` – an inline fragment of computer code. - `
` – preserves whitespace, usually combined with `` for blocks.
- `` – a variable name (e.g., `x`).
- `` – keyboard input (e.g., `Ctrl + C`).
- `` – sample output from a program.

Example: `To print a value, use console.log(x)`. Press `Ctrl+S` to save.

quizData.question: Which tag is suitable for marking up a keyboard shortcut like Ctrl+C?
quizData.explanation: <kbd> represents user input from a keyboard or voice command.
